4.0.0.en: "By the sea side": this happened more than once, and the sea here is the Sea of Galilee. When the crowd pressed upon Christ, the Lord used one of the fishing boats, and sat in it facing the crowds on the shore to teach them. The sea usually signifies the troubled world, and the salt sea, which makes thirsty everyone who drinks from it, and the ship signifies the Church, the source of teaching and of salvation.

4.0.1.en: "In parables": one of the methods that the Lord often used in teaching, and there is also direct preaching, like the Sermon on the Mount. Here He uses a pictorial parable connected with the surroundings and the minds of the people, to make easier the meaning intended to be pictured.

4.1.0.en: "The sower": he is God, and likewise every faithful servant whom God uses in spreading His word (the seed). "Went out": that is, came down and became incarnate for the sake of redemption and the preaching of His word, His seed, some of which fell by the way side and did not sprout, for the fowls of the air came and devoured it up.

4.1.1.en: It is noted that the Lord Christ will return and explain in detail to His disciples the meaning of this parable and the kinds of ground in verses 14-20.

4.2.0.en: And some fell among the stones on rocky soil, and the root could not penetrate the rocks, and the plant died after having sprung up quickly, and the sun burned it, especially since its roots could not supply it with water and nourishment.

4.3.0.en: And some fell into ground that could have yielded fruit, had it not been full of thorns and foreign, useless weeds, which shut out from it the sun and the air, and hindered the roots from growing, so it was choked and died.

4.3.1.en: The last part of the grain fell on good ground, and yielded varied fruit, some thirty, and some sixty, and some a hundred.

4.4.0.en: "He that hath ears to hear": an expression that Christ used more than once, and what is meant by it is a call to the listener to listen well, understand and meditate, not only on the literal meaning, but also on the deeper spiritual meaning.

4.4.1.en: My beloved God ... You were careful that Your word should reach every person so that it might bear its fruit, and for this reason You spoke to all people with every kind of speech so that they might understand ... But what do I do? Why do I not speak with people about You or with Your words, for Your words bring joy and comfort, and understanding them and acting by them is the way to eternity?

4.4.2.en: Grant me, my God, to speak with Your words instead of my own, and with Your wisdom instead of my understanding, so that there may be comfort for me and for others.

4.5.0.en: After the crowds departed, and when He was alone with Christ, the twelve, with some of His followers, asked Him about the meaning of the parable, and He was pleased with them because they asked Him in order to know the spiritual meanings. "Unto you it is given": a special gift and grace that God gives to His faithful servants to understand the hidden and symbolic spiritual meanings, so that they may be filled with them first, and then explain them to others, each according to his capacity.

4.6.0.en: The speech here is a reminder from Christ to His disciples of the prophecy of Isaiah concerning the people who resisted the teaching of the prophet in his time (Isa 6:9-10). What is meant by that is that not everyone who hears, and not everyone who sees, believes the word or understands it, but in many cases does not accept it and resists it, and so man judges himself by that, and does not deserve the forgiveness of sins.

4.7.0.en: The Lord began to explain the parable to them, and made clear that it is simpler than other parables. And He began by saying that God is the Sower, who is careful to cast His word into the hearts of men, and who is able to change man's nature if man wishes it.

4.8.0.en: "The way side": they are those with proud hearts, because the wayside is higher than the field, and has no fence to protect it, that is, no care. And from the many people passing over the way, it becomes hard, so it resembles people who allow evil thoughts to enter into them, so that their hearts are hardened and they do not receive the word of God. Then Satan comes and takes away the word, so it bears no fruit at all.

4.8.1.en: My God ... grant me to be a low and humble field, and not a proud wayside, for Your word knows only the humble heart from which to bring forth fruit.

4.9.0.en: "Stony ground": land with a thin soil that hides within it hard stones, like the hypocritical hearts that show mercy and hide harshness; it also points to the worship of stones, the idols, instead of God. It is land through which the wooden plow, which signifies the Cross, has not passed to break up its hardness, so that its owners may receive the word. And even if these receive the word of God with joy, this is temporary and unstable, and does not stand up against trials or affliction or persecution.

4.10.0.en: "Thorns": those sown among thorns are choked by the cares of the world and its vain material concerns, and the anxiety and delusion that accompany this because of riches. And St. Clement of Alexandria says: "Do not blame money, but its misuse."

4.11.0.en: As for the good ground, they are those who hear and do and bear fruit in graduated measure. It is low (humble) ground, plowed (it carried the Cross), exposed to the sun (that is, it stands before its Christ every day), watered by the Holy Spirit and by His precious Blood ... and we notice the following from this parable:

4.11.1.en: (1) The word of God is available to all, and it is left to man how far he responds to it, or even rejects it. (2) There are levels of being filled and of meditation on the word of God (the disciples), and there is the level of acceptance and understanding (the crowds), and both are acceptable.

4.11.2.en: (3) The kinds of bad ground are three and the good are three, and this reminds us of the parable of the wise and foolish virgins (Mt 25:1-13), in that God's call and grace are one for all. But what about your reaction, beloved?!

4.12.0.en: After explaining the parable to the disciples, Christ continued His speech with a rhetorical question, the purpose of which was to call the disciples to serious preaching work.

4.12.1.en: "Is a candle brought": the candle is the words of Christ, His explanation and His teaching, with which He lit up the hearts and minds of His disciples. And as they were enlightened, they must enlighten the hearts of others with the same words, and this is a responsibility that falls on us also, so we must not be occupied with the world, which the bushel signifies in hiding the word of God, or grow lazy and lie down on the bed, leaving the work of God, but we must lift it high on the candlestick so that the whole world may be lit up with the teaching of Christ. And the candlestick also signifies the Church, shining in the midst of the dark world, for she is responsible for spreading the teaching of Christ. And let us note that the rite of building churches took care to build minarets (towers) in confirmation of this meaning.

4.13.0.en: That is, what I have explained to you privately of the mysteries of the Kingdom is not to hide it, but to proclaim it and teach by it, and that is your responsibility ... And because of the importance of the matter, the Lord Christ repeated what He said to the crowds in (v. 9), that if any man has ears to hear, let him hear.

4.14.0.en: Christ asked His disciples to understand the following truth, namely: the justice of God in the face of the love and labor of His servants. Whoever has offered labor for the spread of the Kingdom and the preaching will receive an added reward, and God gives him here the strength to work. But whoever has no desire to work, even his natural gifts which he did not use will be taken from him here, and he will be punished for his negligence in eternity.

4.15.s.en: (3) The parable of the growing seed and the mustard seed

4.15.0.en: "The kingdom of God": there is a difference between the two expressions "the Kingdom of God" and "the Kingdom of Heaven"...

4.15.1.en: The Kingdom of Heaven means eternity and what follows the Second Coming of Christ. As for the Kingdom of God, it means two things: the first is the spread of faith on earth and the reign of God over the hearts of people, and the second is the work of God in man for the growth of faith within him (ch. 1:14-15).

4.15.2.en: "A man": signifies Christ Himself or the faithful servant who conveys the words of Christ, and the seed is the words of God and His teachings and commandments, and the ground is the heart of man or of mankind in general.

4.16.0.en: "The seed should spring and grow up": a clear reference to the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church and in man, for the Holy Spirit is responsible for spiritual growth in the life of each of us, and for this reason the seed grows in the heart and man responds to it.

4.16.1.en: "He knoweth not how": of course these words refer to the person of the servant who cast the word of God into the hearts, because the responsibility for growth and fruit-bearing is the responsibility of God Himself and not of the servant, as the Apostle Paul said: "Neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase" (1 Cor 3:7).

4.17.0.en: "The earth bringeth forth fruit of herself": a reference to the new nature of mankind after Baptism, in that it is responsive to the work of God and inclined to good. And the Lord Christ makes clear to us here that spiritual growth in the life of man is gradual growth, and not an upheaval and change in a moment ... so it begins as a simple plant at the beginning of repentance, and after that ears, that is, good works, and then it becomes wheat, that is, ripe, steadfast fruit, and likewise it is a source of spiritual food for others.

4.18.0.en: "When the fruit is brought forth": that is, at full ripeness. What is meant is the spread of the Kingdom of God over the hearts of people.

4.18.1.en: "The sickle": a semicircular knife used in harvesting.

4.18.2.en: The general meaning: when the time is fulfilled and at the end of the days, God sends His angels, the reapers (Mt 13:39), to gather this fruit, and people are taken to heaven to be judged for their works.

4.18.3.en: My beloved God ... make me good ground that receives Your word which reaches me, and make me subject to Your Holy Spirit ... for I truly want to grow, and I have nothing but Your work in my life, which I need greatly; establish Your word in me, and occupy my heart with Your love, and make me desire to serve You, and be worthy of Your heavenly Kingdom at Your last coming.

4.19.0.en: A question that Christ asked, not for the purpose of getting an answer from His listeners, but to show us His care to make the truths of the faith clear with simple examples suited to people's minds.

4.20.0.en: Christ's speech here is still connected with the previous speech about the growth of the work of God within man's life, and how, although it begins small in the heart, like one mustard seed, which is the least of all seeds, God's care makes it a great tree with boughs and branches, that is, various spiritual virtues, so that souls without shelter find rest within it.

4.20.1.en: Is this not the Church of God, which appears weak in the eyes of the world? Yet she is the oasis of rest for all who are weary and lost in the world ... So how long, my brother, will you remain a stranger to your Church? Come and take shade, and you will find rest and water and pasture, and your Christ, who awaits you with longing to tend your growth and your fruit-bearing.

4.21.0.en: According to the capacity of the listeners and their understanding, the Lord would speak in parables and comparisons. But privately, that is, with His disciples in their private sessions, He would explain everything to them.

4.22.0.en: On the same day on which Christ spoke in parables, He asked the disciples to cross the Sea of Galilee to the east of the Jordan, so the disciples sent away the crowds, and took the Lord, without preparations, as He was, into the ship. The ship here points to the Church, which always carries her Christ within her, with the Apostles around Him, that is, her fathers and servants.

4.23.0.en: Contrary, violent, opposing winds blew, and they point to the trials and battles to which the soul or the Church is exposed in the world, and the high waves point to the lusts with which Satan tries to fill the soul. And Christ, in all this, did not leave His ship (His Church), but was testing the faith of its servants during the affliction, and showing their weakness and the speed with which they turn to Him. So they awoke Him and reproached Him for neglecting them, instead of asking Him with humility and with confidence in His ability to rescue them.

4.24.0.en: "He rebuked ... and said": ... Christ spoke to the sea and the wind with the authority of a master over his servants, and commanded them to be silent, and the response was immediate and swift, and there was a great calm.

4.25.0.en: Christ's words to the disciples were a rebuke and reproach for their lack of faith in the face of hardship, and for the manner of their speech with Him, which was not fitting. And after the calm, a greater fear came into the hearts of the disciples, and they asked one another about His true identity, and gained a new spiritual experience of the power of Christ, whom the winds and the sea and all nature obey.

4.25.1.en: And we learn from this miracle more than one thing:

4.25.2.en: (1) That the presence of Christ within the Church does not prevent trials and persecutions from occurring.

4.25.3.en: (2) That the purpose of trials in general is a test of faith and of trust in the work of God.

4.25.4.en: (3) God's allowing trials for us is so that we may know our weaknesses, and take refuge in Him, and He rescues us and supports us. (4) That however much boldness there is in our speech with our heavenly Father, it must never be at the expense of respect for the honor of the name of God and awe and fear of Him in our hearts.

4.25.5.en: Chapter 5: the healing of the demoniac, the healing of the woman with the issue of blood, the raising of Jairus' daughter

5.0.s.en: (1) The healing of the demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

5.0.0.en: We find an explanation of this miracle in (Mt 8:28-34), and let us note the following:

5.0.1.en: "The country of the Gadarenes": it is east of the Jordan, and it was a commercial region inhabited by Greeks, and it has another name by which it is known, which is "the country of the Gergesenes."

5.0.2.en: "A man with an unclean spirit": when Christ reached the east of the Sea of Galilee, two demoniacs who lived in the tombs met Him; St. Mark mentioned one of them, who was the more disturbed and raging, and he also made clear the cause of this condition of his, which is that a demon dwelt in him and controlled his actions.

5.1.0.en: "Who had his dwelling among the tombs": a link between Satan and tombs, for the place of Satan is always where death and uncleanness are, and these are the banners of his kingdom. And the speech after this is about the power of Satan and his authority over this soul, so that no one could free him from his authority, or humble this demon and subdue him.

5.1.1.en: "Always, night and day": a picture of the constant torment suffered by the soul which, by its lusts, has put itself under the authority of Satan, so it knows no way of rest, but adds to the wounding of itself by sins (the stones).

5.2.0.en: This man rushed with all his torment toward Christ and worshiped Him, and then the demon cried out, confessing the divinity of the Lord Christ and His truth as the Son of God, and His absolute authority in tormenting him with eternal torment.

5.3.0.en: The speech here is Christ's, for He commanded Satan to leave the man. And the reason for Christ's asking the name of the demon was not that it was hidden from Him, but to teach us about the ferocity of Satan and his harshness in possessing the soul, and then the power of His authority over the whole kingdom of demons, however many they may be.

5.4.0.en: "And he besought him much": it is not easy for Satan in his pride to declare his defeat, despite his confessing Christ's authority over him, and for this reason he asked not to be sent away out of the country, that is, the place. And because Satan knew that Christ would surely cast him out of the man, he asked instead to enter into a herd of swine, which are among the unclean animals in the law of the Old Testament.

5.5.0.en: "Gave them leave": it makes clear to us that however great Satan's power, he can do nothing unless God permits it.

5.5.1.en: Why did Christ give leave?!: perhaps the reader asks why He allowed Satan to enter the herd of swine, and to drive them wild and push them toward the sea, and about two thousand were drowned, which was the number of the whole herd?! Christ allowed this as a chastisement of the owners of the swine, who had raised them in violation of God's commandment, and sold them at cheap prices that tempted people to buy them ... So Christ's punishment was just against one who violated the Law and made people stumble.

5.6.0.en: The herdsmen went out in panic and terror to the owners of the herd, and of course they told everyone they met in the cities and their suburbs, so everyone went out to see and to verify. And when they came to the place where the Lord was, they found the demoniac in a new condition to which they were not accustomed ... calm ... sitting ... in his right mind ... and the crowd who had seen the miracle began to tell it to those who had not seen it. But the owners of the swine, to whom the swine mattered more than the man, were distressed by the loss of the herd, and asked the Lord to leave the place!!

5.7.0.en: As gratitude, and out of a sincere desire, the man who had been healed wanted to follow Christ and to go into the ship with Him. But the Lord Christ prevented him, and asked something else of him: first, that he go to his household so that they might be comforted by his return in health ... second, that he bear witness to God and His work in his healing.

5.7.1.en: And the man obeyed, and began to proclaim and tell all people what Christ had done for him.

5.7.2.en: "Decapolis": the region east of the Sea of Galilee, of which the country of the Gadarenes was one. See also the commentary on (Mt 4:24-25).

5.7.3.en: We learn from this man something important, which is that man must submit his will to God and not cling to his own opinion ... We present our desires to our Father, yes, but we leave the choice to Him ... for the man's desire was a blessed desire, which was to be with Christ ... but Christ charged him with another service, and he rejoiced in it, and set out to serve diligently ... So let us also learn not to hold fast to our opinions, and to leave the leading of our lives to the wisdom and choice of our God.

5.8.s.en: (2) The meeting with Jairus and the healing of the woman with the issue of blood

5.8.0.en: "The other side": it is the western side of the sea, to which Christ returned after the miracle of the healing of the demoniac. And as usual, the crowds either followed Him or were waiting for Him on His arrival.

5.9.0.en: "One of the rulers of the synagogue": that is, one of the elders of the Jews of high standing from the religious and social side, and the name Jairus means "enlightened," and he represents the Jew enlightened by the Law, so he believes in Christ and worships Him.

5.9.1.en: "He besought him greatly": that is, he asked with urgency, which makes clear the bad condition of the daughter on one hand, and the tender fatherhood of Jairus and his desire for her healing on the other, placing his last hopes in Christ's visit to her, and his courteous manner in asking, since he first worshiped Christ, then entreated Him saying: "Come and lay thy hands on her ... that she may live." And when Christ saw these feelings, He went with him. And as usual, the crowds followed Him, thronging. My beloved God ... how sweet are the words that Jairus uttered, "Come." Yes, my Lord, come and lay Your hand on me so that I may be cleansed from my sins and healed of my weaknesses ... come to free me from material things and the love of the world.

5.9.2.en: My beloved brother ... make this petition that Jairus uttered a prayer between your lips, so that in every feeling of weakness or weariness or distress you say: "Come, my Lord Jesus."

5.10.0.en: On the way to the house of Jairus, Christ met the woman with the issue of blood (see Mt 9:

5.10.1.en: 20), whose condition St. Mark explained in detail as an introduction to the miracle.

5.10.2.en: "Twelve years": that is, the fullness of the time of her pain and of her psychological suffering besides the bodily, since a woman with a flow of blood was considered unclean and could not approach the temple or perform religious practices; and what also would be the state of a body after bleeding for so long a time as this?!

5.10.3.en: "Physicians ... spent ... worse": St. Mark continues to draw her picture, for she was in despair after going through the physicians and trying all the medicines, and she was poor since she had spent all her money, and her condition became worse, that is, the pains increased and money and medicine were unable to heal her, pointing to the helplessness of men, with all their capabilities, and the need for Christ the Savior.

5.11.0.en: "When she had heard": her case was like that of many who heard about Christ and His miracles of healing, and not only her need or her despair of healing moved her, but there was also a faith that moved her, for she said within herself: "If I may touch," and it was a simple faith, and it also reveals to us her respect for the commandment of the Law in not touching a person because of her uncleanness, so she took a decision to touch nothing but His clothes.

5.12.0.en: The moment of her touching the clothes of the Savior was the moment of her healing, and she felt a wonderful new power running through her body.

5.12.1.en: My beloved brother ... do you not ask with me how the woman with the issue of blood was healed without even asking?! It is the simple, humble faith that many have lost in these days!! Her sense of unworthiness made her come from behind Him and be ashamed to ask, and her faith made her press through the crowd, despite the weakness of her body, so she obtained what she wanted. O my God, grant me to be like her in her virtues: believing ... humble ... persevering ... striving.

5.13.0.en: "The virtue had gone out": an expression of the Lord Christ's awareness of what had happened. And the word "gone out" means that He is the one with authority over healing and the giver of it, and not His bare clothes. My beloved brother ... the established tradition in our Church teaches the honoring of the bodies and relics of the saints, and the keeping in our churches of some of their relics ... and people are blessed by touching them and by seeking their intercession for healing or the receiving of a blessing.

5.13.1.en: And to those who oppose this tradition, we say that the clothes of Christ carried all His power ... so also the relics of the saints carry the power of God Himself, for the Healer in every case is God with His full authority, but He gives honor to the names of His holy children.

5.13.2.en: "Who touched my clothes?": of course Christ knew who had touched His clothes, but by this question He wanted two things: the second: the proclaiming of the miracle itself to everyone.

5.13.3.en: The first: the proclaiming of the faith of the humble woman.

5.13.4.en: But because the disciples did not understand the Lord's purpose, they asked in wonder: Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?! But Christ continued to look around, giving the woman an opportunity to declare herself.

5.14.0.en: The woman understood well that she was the one meant by Christ's words and no other, and this increased her fear and confusion, but it did not prevent her from coming forward and confessing the truth, for her human weakness did not push her to flee, but she confessed the truth. And Christ's reply to her was reassuring, removing all anxiety, for He praised her faith and made clear that it was the cause of her healing, and blessed her, and commanded for her the continuance of the healing.

5.14.1.en: My Lord Jesus ... grant me the courage of the woman with the issue of blood, so that I may draw near to You to obtain the lasting healing from my sins.

5.15.0.en: The return here is to the story of Jairus' sick daughter, after the end of the healing of the woman with the issue of blood ... for on the way of Jairus' return to his house, some people came from his house to tell him of his daughter's death, and that there was therefore no need for Christ to come, for no one imagined that Christ could do anything with death; but Christ intervened in the conversation, and spoke directly with Jairus, and encouraged him, saying to him: "Be not afraid," and He also gave him the only weapon for driving out fear, which is faith.

5.16.0.en: "And he suffered no man": ... the crowd followed Him to the house of Jairus, but when entering the house, Christ did not allow anyone to enter except Peter and James and John of the disciples, and these three are the ones whom He also took with Him on the Mount of Transfiguration (ch. 9), and likewise in Gethsemane on the night of His crucifixion.

5.17.0.en: And as is expected in these circumstances, especially because of the young age of the daughter, the grief and weeping and wailing were great, and Christ surprised them with a question and a truth that astonished the crowd and the family. "Why make ye this ado, and weep?": a question that seems strange in such a situation ... and can anything else be done but weep?!

5.17.1.en: "The damsel is not dead": and this is the truth that cannot be believed, for the death was plain and real, and the crowds were witnesses to it, and can we not tell the difference between sleep and death?!

5.17.2.en: "They laughed him to scorn": it seems that they wondered at or mocked the words of Christ, since they were sure of the death of the girl, but Christ took her parents with the three disciples, and entered the room where the girl lay.

5.18.0.en: Christ took the girl by the hand, and called her with the command to arise from her death, and He alone is the One with authority over death. And the phrase "Talitha cumi" was a widespread Syriac expression, which St. Mark took care to mention as Christ pronounced it, and then translated into its meaning: "Damsel, I say unto thee, arise."

5.19.0.en: "Arose, and walked": that is, she returned to full health, and did not go through a period of convalescence, for example, that is, the resurrection and healing were accomplished, and everyone was amazed with a wondrous amazement, for what had happened was beyond the belief of any mind. "He charged them straitly that no man should know it": such news cannot be kept quiet, for St. Matthew mentioned that: "The fame hereof went abroad into all that land" (9:26). As for Christ's request, its cause was perhaps the desire not to arouse the envy of the rulers against Him, or that people's faith in Him should be from conviction and not from excitement at the miracles ... and He asked that something be given her to eat, and this is also a confirmation that her resurrection was in her real body and not an illusion.

5.19.1.en: The entering of Christ into the house of Jairus turned grief into joy, and He still stands at the doors of our hearts, and we still want Him to raise up everyone who has died by sin, and to restore joy to the heart instead of gloom and grief ... Open to Him, beloved, speak with Him and tell Him that you need Him to touch you with His hand to raise you up sound in repentance, and to give you to eat of His true Body and Blood, declaring your healing and your resurrection.

5.19.2.en: Christ's preaching, the preaching of the disciples, the beheading of John, the two miracles of feeding the crowds, the miracle of walking on the water
